title: Language models identify viral regions less prone to immune escape
summary: Analysis of influenza, HIV, and coronavirus sequences identifies regions of surface proteins less likely to mutate to escape immune responses, including the S2 subunit of spike. These are computational leads for studying possible vaccine targets, not validated vaccines.

evidence.tested: Language models trained on about 60,000 HIV, 45,000 influenza and 4,000 coronavirus sequences were checked against earlier findings on influenza and HIV; the SARS-CoV-2 analysis is described as not yet peer-reviewed.
evidence.unknown: Flagged SARS-CoV-2 sequences still need investigation, and it is unknown how fast SARS-CoV-2 mutates, so how long current vaccines stay effective is unclear.
evidence.ai_role: Adapted language-model methods to viral protein sequences to predict surface regions more or less likely to enable immune escape, as candidate vaccine targets.
